correctness.rationale: Exact R²=varphi+2 regular polar normal model, silhouette-edge count for every feasible six-axis sign chamber, certified 32 feasible chambers of which 20 have twelve projected vertices. Exact Z[varphi] checker verifies each triangular q norm, inward conormal product, and endpoint norm. Green identities Δh=−2h and Δh²=2|q|²−6h² yield precisely the weighted first and second moments. The known unconditional moments give the ten-vertex counterparts, and elementary alternating-arctangent inequalities rigorously prove negative covariance. Packaged checker passed actual exact enumeration, 400 convex-hull comparisons, and supplementary 240k-point sphere quadrature.

originality.rationale: The complete prior unweighted type law, Platonic unconditional brightness moments, six-circle tessellation, and the already-used spherical flux method were explicitly excluded from originality. The inspected full primary texts and search results did not yield the dodecahedron-specific type-weighted first and second area moments or the strict negative covariance; the general tetrahedral formulas do not imply values for a twelve-facet dodecahedron. The identified historical-priority risk remains real.
residual_risks: Historical stereology, light-projection, or classical dodecahedral shadow papers not fully indexed or accessible could contain an equivalent conditional moment identity.
The marginal ten/twelve law and unconditional variance are already prior-covered and must not be used as independent novelty evidence.
The spherical boundary-flux integration method was used for tetrahedral shadow moments; no novelty is asserted for that technique itself.

value.rationale: Complete first and second area moments conditioned on both possible silhouette combinatorial types of the regular dodecahedron answer a natural joint stereological question not resolved by separate brightness and combinatorial marginals. The strict negative association and separate conditional variances show how view complexity and observed area differ for a classical Platonic solid; exact dodecahedral normal-fan evaluation has standalone value even without a universal theorem.
